prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Baytown, Texas, and has back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1029; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recording is for our claim file. Can you state your full name for the record?

A: I'd rather just go by my initials for now, if that's okay.

Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?

A: I was driving through Baytown, Texas, on a weekday afternoon. Traffic had slowed down ahead of a light, so I was already stopped when it happened.

Q: Understood. What happened next?

A: The car behind me didn't stop in time. I felt a hard jolt from the back, and my head snapped forward and then back against the seat.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?

A: Yes, I was.

Q: Did you get out of the vehicle at the scene?

A: I did, but I felt stiff almost right away. I walked around for a minute and then sat down on the curb because my lower back was tightening up.

Q: Did you seek medical attention?

A: I went to an urgent care clinic later that evening. They examined my back and told me I had a lumbar strain. They gave me a muscle relaxer and told me to rest and avoid heavy lifting.

Q: Have you had any prior problems with your back?

A: Nothing serious. I've had occasional soreness after long days on my feet, but nothing that stopped me from working.

Q: How are you feeling at the moment?

A: Better than the first few days, but I still get a sharp ache when I bend over or sit for a long time. I've been doing gentle stretches as the clinic suggested.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?

A: Only that I want to cooperate fully and get this resolved. I'll send over any follow-up paperwork from the clinic.

Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
